cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T5 attacks T4's trial on cost; T6 answers that cost directly.
cells.limitation: T4 answers T3 with 'test beats a hunch' and sidesteps its combination hypothesis.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T8 introduces sting-versus-severe-reaction limit; T9 builds its testing boundary on it.
cells.limitation: T7's pre-set reaction criteria and T9's moment-bound verdict never get used later.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T5-T6 weigh the cost of another reaction against the cost of not knowing.
cells.limitation: Nobody raises comparing ingredient lists or known stinging actives as a cheap first check.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T6 reshapes the test plan into a prioritized patch trial after T5.
cells.limitation: Skeptic's combination point (T3, T10) never reshapes the Experimenter's one-at-a-time method.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D separates calming the skin from finding the cause, with combination left open.
cells.limitation: Section D calls stopping 'informative on its own', blurring T2's point that it isolates nothing.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T6 grants T5's strongest point, 'Testing everything is greedy', before countering.
cells.limitation: T4 recasts T3's combination and weather alternatives as a mere hunch.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T10 names the single-culprit assumption and says the clean experiment breaks if false.
cells.limitation: T10's challenge, the sharpest, gets no answer from either target.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T8's red flags (swelling, blistering, spreading rash) are accurate escalation signs.
cells.limitation: T7 assumes a 'serum' the user never mentioned; Section D contradicts T2 on stopping.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T3 offers combination, weather, old face wash as possibilities, not findings.
cells.limitation: T1 asserts removal 'helps whatever the cause' without marking it as a judgment.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T9 accepts T8's boundary and narrows its own claim to mild stings.
cells.limitation: Experimenter never concedes or answers the combination objection from T3 and T10.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A names cause, combination or unrelated factor, plus severity as the uncertainty.
cells.limitation: Section D's closing question drifts from finding the cause toward product attachment.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T5 uses the three-product count to propose keeping only the one valued most.
cells.limitation: The one-week onset timing never informs the reasoning about delayed or cumulative irritation.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T6 keeps the user's goal of identifying the cause against T5's skip-testing stance.
cells.limitation: T5 would leave the cause unknown although the user asked how to find it.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T8 and Section E set clear medical escalation stakes for severe reactions.
cells.limitation: T3 adds 'cold weather' and T7 a 'serum' as context the user never gave.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on severity, fading after pause, persistence, and layering.
cells.limitation: Which products or actives were used is never asked, though it decides the plan.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section D asks which product the user would most hate to lose.
cells.limitation: No alternative motives offered, such as why three products began at once.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3 exposes the assumption that the newest, strongest-sounding product is guilty.
cells.limitation: T10 surfaces the single-culprit assumption only in the last turn, unexplored.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T5 sets knowing the cause against avoiding a second reaction.
cells.limitation: Section D's value question is not tied back to how much testing to do.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T7 notes expectation can make a faint tingle feel like proof.
cells.limitation: The user's worry about skin damage is never acknowledged beyond triage in T8.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E gives conditional branches the user can apply to their own skin.
cells.limitation: Section D offers a single reflective question, with no alternatives to choose between.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Options: stop all (T1), reintroduce singly (T2), keep one (T5), clinician (T8).
cells.limitation: No turn frames the pause length or when reintroduction should begin.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T5 and T6 state costs of testing and of skipping tests.
cells.limitation: Stopping all three is treated as costless in T1; lost benefits go unmentioned.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: sting fading after pause favors reintroduction; layering-only reaction favors fewer products.
cells.limitation: Section E's 'a week or two' and 'a few days apart' are not from user facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section E separates severity, the consequential unknown, from which product is responsible.
cells.limitation: Unknown product identities are not weighed as a consequential unknown in Sections D-E.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: T7's written criteria and T6's small-patch reintroduction fit a mild sting.
cells.limitation: Section E orders reintroduction by value, not by likely irritancy of each product.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T8: 'pain rather than sting' draws a plain, usable line.
cells.limitation: T2's falsification maxim is slightly abstract for a skincare question.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T9 'That sets a boundary' plainly refers to T8; T10 'You two' is clear.
cells.limitation: Section D's 'informative on its own' traces to no turn and conflicts with T2.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Ten turns, all within range, each making one move.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Explicit shifts: T6 'I concede part of that', T9 'I accept it'.
cells.limitation: All three minds share a calm, measured register; voices differ mainly by stance.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: T8 builds on T7's notes in one clause before adding its limit.
cells.limitation: T10 largely restates T3's combination idea rather than advancing it.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T8 raises allergic reaction or chemical burn against curiosity.
cells.limitation: Tension stays procedural; the stakes for the user's face are rarely felt in T1-T7.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T6 concedes 'Testing everything is greedy', citing T5's cost-of-reaction argument.
cells.limitation: Concessions are partial and expected; no position surprises after T6.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T4: 'Hunches never risk being wrong; tests do.'
cells.limitation: The Subtractor in T1, T5, T8 lacks a distinctive voice beyond caution.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T5: 'A missing answer is cheaper than a second reaction.'
cells.limitation: No analogy or vivid example; lines are crisp but plain throughout.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T10 ends on live disagreement that the synthesis carries forward.
cells.limitation: Rhythm stays even across T1-T10, with little rise or release.

strengths: T8 and Section E set clear, accurate escalation signs separating a testable sting from a medical reaction.
T5-T6 trade real costs of testing against skipping, with a caused concession in T6.
Section E gives observable conditions (fading, persistence, layering-only reaction) each tied to an option.
weaknesses: The debate never asks which products or actives were used, the fact that most shapes the plan (T2-T6).
The Story Skeptic's combination hypothesis (T3, T10) never reshapes the Experimenter's one-at-a-time method.
Motives and fears get little attention; Section D's single question is the only reflective prompt.

symptoms.observed: Product identities and ingredients never asked; plan proceeds without them.
symptoms.evidence: you have not said which products

symptoms.observed: Ingredient-label comparison or known stinging actives never raised as a cheap check.
symptoms.evidence: reintroduce one product at a time

symptoms.observed: Combination hypothesis raised twice; Experimenter never adapts the method to it.
symptoms.evidence: irritation can come from stacking several fine products

symptoms.observed: No alternative motives offered; only attachment to one product touched.
symptoms.evidence: Keep the one you care about most

symptoms.observed: User's worry about damage only appears as triage, not acknowledged.
symptoms.evidence: Curiosity should not outrank a real allergic reaction

findings.description: T7 names a serum and T3 cold weather; neither appears in the user's situation.
Says stopping is informative on its own, contradicting T2 that stopping isolates no product.
Popper, Taleb and Kahneman attributions are paraphrases consistent with the works; not checkable here.

rubric_fit_notes: Criterion 4 fits a skincare troubleshooting question loosely; motives and outside expectations have limited room, so C4 cells read the reflective opportunity actually available. The ungrounded_number pattern sits in Section E, not a turn, so its turns list is empty.
